records.title: SQLite Session Extension introduction
records.release_or_commit: SQLite documentation; 3.54.0 current release context recorded at access (S06); page version not separately tagged
records.locator: Sections describing changesets/patchsets, enabling the extension, and limitations

access_utc.precision: batch retrieval interval; per-page timestamp unavailable

records.observed_operation: Read primary documentation for session-generated database changesets and patchsets.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Session extension is disabled by default and requires SQLITE_ENABLE_SESSION and SQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK. Changesets apply against compatible schema/database state; only tables with declared primary keys are tracked, NULL primary-key rows are ignored, and virtual tables are unsupported.
records.applicability: Optional row-delta transport for an SQLite implementation, not an append-only domain event log or policy for semantic conflicts.

access_utc.precision: batch retrieval interval; per-page timestamp unavailable

records.observed_operation: Read API details for session capture, applying a changeset, and conflict handling.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Changeset application invokes conflict handling that can omit, abort, or replace conflicting changes. Repeated edits within one session coalesce; reverted changes can disappear. The consumer must supply handling behavior and compatible schema.
records.applicability: Useful only if the selected build enables the extension and the application separately records durable event history and user-facing merge decisions.

records.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
records.release_or_commit: SQLite documentation; version context S06; page version not separately tagged
records.locator: WAL persistence, synchronous behavior, and WAL limitations sections

access_utc.precision: batch retrieval interval; per-page timestamp unavailable

records.observed_operation: Read official WAL behavior and documented deployment limits.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL with synchronous=FULL synchronizes the WAL on each commit; NORMAL may lose a recently committed transaction after OS crash or power loss. WAL requires participating processes on the same host and is not suitable as a cross-host/network-filesystem synchronization mechanism; active database state includes the WAL sidecar.
records.applicability: Potential local store durability baseline only; it is not the multi-laptop replication protocol. Actual guarantees depend on filesystem/device behavior.

records.observed_operation: Read documented durability settings and their conditions.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Durability behavior is controlled by synchronous mode and journal mode; NORMAL and FULL have different sync frequency and crash-loss properties. The selected setting must be applied and verified for the chosen build/database.
records.applicability: Supports a deliberate local durability decision; does not by itself guarantee hardware honors flushes or recover external media files.

records.title: CouchDB conflict handling
records.release_or_commit: CouchDB 3.5.x stable documentation; exact rendered build/package version not pinned (UNKNOWN)
records.locator: Conflict detection and resolution; winner selection; tombstones and revision history sections

access_utc.precision: batch retrieval interval; per-page timestamp unavailable

records.observed_operation: Read official replication-conflict documentation.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Replicas can retain conflicting leaf revisions; deterministic winner is returned in ordinary access while _conflicts/open_revs can expose alternatives. Deletions propagate as tombstones. Compaction/pruning can remove old non-leaf bodies; revision trees are not an application audit log.
records.applicability: Useful replication candidate if all relevant conflict leaves are surfaced and app policy is layered on top; pin the server release and retention behavior.

records.title: CouchDB replication introduction
records.release_or_commit: CouchDB 3.5.x stable documentation; exact rendered build/package version not pinned (UNKNOWN)
records.locator: Replication direction, checkpoints, deletion, and filtering sections

access_utc.precision: batch retrieval interval; per-page timestamp unavailable

records.observed_operation: Read official replication overview for push/pull behavior and recovery conditions.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: One-way replication pushes or pulls; configuring both directions supports bidirectional exchange. Checkpoints permit resumption and deletions replicate. Content-dependent filters may mishandle deleted docs; a _deleted:true document retaining body can preserve attachment data.
records.applicability: Supports a sync option but requires explicit deletion/filter policy and media-transfer controls.

records.observed_operation: Read official attachment API for metadata versus byte transfer.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Attachment stubs/metadata can refer to content while attachment requests or replication transfer bytes. Keeping photo bytes outside replicated documents avoids implicit content replication only if app/replication configuration also enforces that separation.
records.applicability: Supports a manifest/reference design; never infer that references alone prevent a configured replicator from moving bytes.
